claims.text: W-Ta-Cr-V is a refractory high-entropy alloy developed for high-temperature and irradiation-exposed applications.
The W-Ta-Cr-V alloy forms Cr- and V-rich precipitates.
The Cr- and V-rich precipitates develop specifically under combined temperatures of at least 1000°C and irradiation exposure.
Cr- and V-rich precipitates can embrittle the W-Ta-Cr-V alloy.
Cr- and V-rich precipitates reduce both ductility and strength.

The baseline W-Ta-Cr-V alloy has favorable resistance to ion irradiation and helium implantation, including no noticeable dislocation-loop formation, smaller helium bubbles, and no radiation-induced grain-boundary segregation.
Adding approximately 1-5 atomic percent Hf to W-Ta-Cr-V forms a quinary alloy.
A minor Hf addition will reduce or suppress Cr- and V-rich precipitates.
Hf addition will modify phase stability and elemental partitioning in the W-Ta-Cr-V alloy.
Hf addition may refine or stabilize grain boundaries.
Hf changes the thermodynamic balance and reduces the driving force for Cr/V segregation and precipitation during high-temperature exposure.
Suppression of Cr/V segregation and precipitation preserves a stable microstructure under irradiation.
The Hf-modified alloy will have higher yield strength than baseline W-Ta-Cr-V under identical high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
The Hf-modified alloy will have greater ductility than baseline W-Ta-Cr-V under identical high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
The Hf-modified alloy will maintain thermal and irradiation resistance comparable to the baseline alloy.
A quinary derivative of W-Ta-Cr-V has been reported to have improved resistance to high-temperature and irradiation environments.
The proposed benefit should hold at temperatures of at least 1000°C under heavy-ion irradiation and helium implantation.
Excess or nonoptimal Hf may generate unwanted secondary phases or compromise oxidation resistance.
